newsitem.title: USA: USDA says vegetable imports via JFK steady in Marc.
newsitem.headline: USDA says vegetable imports via JFK steady in Marc.

text.p: Fresh vegetable imports via John F. Kennedy airport were fairly steady at 391,545 cartons in March, the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) said.
This was little changed from 390,411 cartons in the same 1996 period.
George Jelinek, USDA Port Director, said the perishables comprised 30 to 40 different types of fruit and vegetables, including eggplant, peppers and tomatoes.
He told Reuters that Israel, Netherlands and the Dominican Republic were the top three countries of origin for perishable exports to JFK during 1996 and "it would probably remain the same for 1997."
Israel exported 119,990 cartons of fresh fruit and vegetables destined for U.S. sale via JFK in March, of which 92,903 cartons were tomatoes.
Netherlands exported 33,898 cartons overall, the USDA said. Some 24,868 cartons comprised tomatoes, the top imported perishable commodity in March.
The Dominican Republic exported 23,659 cartons of vegetables via JFK in March, including 1,445 cartons of tomatoes.
Spain moved 163,895 cartons of tomatoes though JFK during the month, all of which were destined to Canada.
